text:
Four goals on chances worth between 14 and 23 percent each, and Boston still walked off down 4-1 in a game it arguably played even. The expected goals finished OTT 2.46, BOS 2.41, and the deserved-to-win split was 51 percent for Ottawa and 49 for Boston. The scoreboard had far more daylight than the play did.

Ottawa made its lead early. Tim Stützle scored a shorthanded snap shot at 7:39 of the first, then another snap shot at 9:22 to make it 2-0. Drake Batherson added a backhand at 1:06 of the second, and Michael Amadio's snap shot at 5:19 made it 4-0, the best of the four looks at 23 percent. Jeremy Swayman faced 24 shots and allowed four against 2.46 expected, which cost Boston about 1.5 goals compared with an average goalie. Stützle finished with two goals and an assist, and Amadio had a goal and an assist.

Boston dominated the third, out-chancing Ottawa 0.86 to 0.28 in expected goals, but the only reward was James Hagens' snap shot at 3:30 on a 2 percent chance, the least likely goal of the night. Linus Ullmark stopped all 10 shots he faced, about 1.6 goals better than expected. Neither team converted on four power plays, and Boston took 28 penalty minutes to Ottawa's 18.
